strategy: trait-driven dispatch via separate capabilities table — zero modifications to upstream ggml.c type_traits[] array, zero modifications to upstream struct fields

upstream_files_never_touched: ggml/src/ggml.c (type_traits[] array, quantize_* switch — only append new enum + new cases)
append_only_files: ggml/include/ggml.h (add struct + API at end, add enum types at end)
ggml/src/ggml.c (append type_traits entries + dispatch cases — never modify existing lines)
ggml/src/CMakeLists.txt (append new .c files to source list)
one_time_refactor_files: src/llama-kv-cache.cpp (15 hardcoded type checks → trait lookups — done ONCE, then never conflicts with upstream again)
src/llama-graph.cpp (12 hardcoded type checks → trait lookups — done ONCE, then never conflicts again)

builder_instructions.overview: Fork TheTom's feature/turboquant-kv-cache (has turbo3/4/2 KV-cache architecture). Implement a separate ggml_quant_caps capabilities table so ALL type-specific behavior in kv-cache and graph is data-driven. Then port planar/iso quants, deferred allocation, weight compression, HRM architect, hidden state API, and stability modules on top of the modular base. Adding a future quant type = 1 new .c file + 1 caps table entry + 1 type_traits entry + 1 dispatch case. Zero changes to kv-cache.cpp or graph.cpp.

phases.name: fork_and_baseline
phases.description: Fork TheTom's repo at feature/turboquant-kv-cache. Clone, build, verify baseline compiles before any changes.
steps: Configure: cmake -B build -DGGML_CUDA=ON (or OFF for CPU-only)
validation: No new compiler errors or warnings vs baseline

phases.name: create_capabilities_table
phases.description: Create a SEPARATE capabilities struct and table. This does NOT modify the existing ggml_type_traits struct or the type_traits[] array in ggml.c. It is a parallel data structure that higher-level code (kv-cache, graph) queries instead of hardcoding type checks.
phases.principle: The existing ggml_type_traits has quantization function pointers (to_float, from_float_ref). The NEW ggml_quant_caps has SEMANTIC capabilities (needs_wht, needs_deferred, head_align). Higher-level code uses caps for behavioral decisions, traits for quantization operations. Never mix them.

create.description: Public header: caps struct definition + accessor API
Capabilities table. ONE source of truth for all type-specific behavior. Add a new quant type by appending ONE entry here.

modify.instruction: Add ggml-quant-caps.c to the GGML_CPU_SOURCES list (or equivalent variable). Append after the existing turbo quant sources. Example: add 'ggml-quant-caps.c' to the list.
Add #include "ggml-quant-caps.h" at the end of the includes section (before the closing #ifdef/__cplusplus). This is append-only — do NOT modify any existing lines.

validation: The caps table compiles. No warnings about unused fields.

phases.name: refactor_kv_cache_to_caps
phases.description: Replace ALL 15 hardcoded type checks in llama-kv-cache.cpp with ggml_quant_caps lookups. This is a ONE-TIME refactor. After this, adding new quant types requires ZERO changes to kv-cache.cpp.
phases.principle: Every 'if (type == TURBO3 || type == TURBO4 || ...)' becomes a caps lookup. Use the specific predicate that matches the SEMANTIC intent of each check, not just the type list.
phases.critical_note: Some checks look similar but have different semantics. Read the BEFORE/AFTER carefully. The variable names in the code (is_turbo, k_is_turbo, v_is_turbo) are misleading — what matters is the behavioral intent of each check.

refactor_sites.semantic: FAMILY CHECK: does type_k use WHT rotation?
refactor_sites.search_pattern: const bool k_is_turbo = (type_k == GGML_TYPE_TURBO3_0 || type_k == GGML_TYPE_TURBO4_0 || type_k == GGML_TYPE_TURBO2_0);
refactor_sites.note: This is inside the constructor body. May need to add #include "ggml-quant-caps.h" at top of file.

refactor_sites.semantic: SPECIFIC TYPE CHECK: only turbo2 triggers this mode
refactor_sites.replace_with: NO CHANGE — keep hardcoded. This checks a SPECIFIC type, not a family.
refactor_sites.note: This is a specific-type trigger, not a family check. Leave as-is.

refactor_sites.semantic: FAMILY CHECK: does type_k need WHT? Used for adaptive modes 1/2 (set K+V to Q8_0)
refactor_sites.search_pattern: const bool is_turbo = (type_k == GGML_TYPE_TURBO3_0 || type_k == GGML_TYPE_TURBO4_0 || type_k == GGML_TYPE_TURBO2_0 || type_k == GGML_TYPE_PLANAR3_0 || type_k == GGML_TYPE_ISO3_0 || type_k == GGML_TYPE_PLANAR4_0 || type_k == GGML_TYPE_ISO4_0);
refactor_sites.note: In the base fork (TheTom's), this line may only have turbo3/4/2 (no planar/iso yet). That's fine — replace with the predicate anyway. When planar/iso are ported in Phase 4, their caps entry will have needs_wht=true and they'll automatically be included.

refactor_sites.semantic: TURBO FAMILY ONLY: used for V adaptive modes 5/6/7 which set V to turbo4/turbo2
refactor_sites.search_pattern: const bool v_is_turbo = (type_v == GGML_TYPE_TURBO3_0 || type_v == GGML_TYPE_TURBO4_0 || type_v == GGML_TYPE_TURBO2_0);
refactor_sites.note: This is turbo_family, NOT needs_wht. V adaptive modes set V to specific turbo types (turbo4/turbo2). Planar/iso do NOT participate.

refactor_sites.semantic: FAMILY CHECK: does layer_type_k need head_dim alignment?
refactor_sites.search_pattern: const bool k_is_turbo = (layer_type_k == GGML_TYPE_TURBO3_0 || layer_type_k == GGML_TYPE_TURBO4_0 || layer_type_k == GGML_TYPE_TURBO2_0 || layer_type_k == GGML_TYPE_PLANAR3_0 || ...);
refactor_sites.note: Replace the boolean + if-check together. The padding logic follows (padded_head_k calculation). Adjust the if-condition to use k_head_align instead of 'k_is_turbo && n_embd_head_k % 128 != 0'.

refactor_sites.semantic: FAMILY CHECK: does layer_type_v need head_dim alignment?
refactor_sites.note: Same pattern as KV-5 but for V. Note: uses needs_wht (all WHT types need padding), NOT turbo_family. In the base fork this may only list turbo types — that's fine, the predicate will match when planar/iso are ported.

refactor_sites.semantic: DEFERRED CHECK: does layer_type_k need F16-during-prefill?
refactor_sites.note: In the base fork, this code doesn't exist yet (no planar/iso). This site is created in Phase 5 when porting deferred allocation. Listed here for completeness.

refactor_sites.semantic: FAMILY CHECK: does type_k need WHT rotation matrices?
refactor_sites.search_pattern: if (turbo_rotation == nullptr &&\n            \(type_k == GGML_TYPE_TURBO3_0 || type_k == GGML_TYPE_TURBO4_0 || type_k == GGML_TYPE_TURBO2_0\))
refactor_sites.note: The rotation matrices (turbo_rotation, turbo_rotation_inv, turbo_innerq_scale_inv) are shared across ALL WHT-family types. Using needs_wht means planar/iso automatically get them.

refactor_sites.semantic: FAMILY CHECK: does the RUNTIME tensor type need WHT handling?
refactor_sites.note: These check the ACTUAL tensor type at runtime (after deferred conversion, the tensor type is the quant type). Using needs_wht handles all WHT-family types uniformly.

modify.instruction: Add #include "ggml-quant-caps.h" at the top of the file (after existing ggml includes). Then apply all refactor sites KV-1 through KV-12. Search for each search_pattern and replace with replace_with. For sites marked 'NO CHANGE', skip them.

validation: grep -c 'GGML_TYPE_TURBO3_0.*GGML_TYPE_TURBO4_0.*GGML_TYPE_TURBO2_0' src/llama-kv-cache.cpp returns 0 (all family checks replaced)

The ONLY remaining hardcoded type checks in kv-cache.cpp should be: KV-2 (type_v == TURBO2_0 Boundary V trigger), and the adaptive mode assignments (layer_type_v = GGML_TYPE_TURBO4_0 etc. — these SET types, not CHECK them)

phases.name: refactor_graph_to_caps
phases.description: Replace ALL 12 hardcoded type checks in llama-graph.cpp with caps lookups. Same one-time refactor principle.
phases.principle: All 12 sites in graph.cpp check for turbo3/4/2 only (NOT planar/iso). These are turbo-family-specific attention/rotation operations. Use turbo_family predicate to match current behavior exactly. When planar/iso attention support is added later, add a separate registration — do NOT blanket-enable them here.

Replace all 6 individually. Some check k->type, some check v->type. Match the variable in the replacement.

phases.name: port_planar_iso_quants
phases.description: Port the PlanarQuant (planar3/4) and IsoQuant (iso3/4) implementations from the source repo. This adds 4 new quant types. Thanks to the modular caps system, NO changes to kv-cache.cpp or graph.cpp are needed — just the quant files, traits entries, and caps entries.
steps_in_order: 1. Add 4 enum values to ggml.h: GGML_TYPE_PLANAR3_0, GGML_TYPE_ISO3_0, GGML_TYPE_PLANAR4_0, GGML_TYPE_ISO4_0 (append before GGML_TYPE_COUNT, increment GGML_TYPE_COUNT)
2. Add block structs to ggml-common.h: block_planar3_0, block_iso3_0, block_planar4_0, block_iso4_0 + QK_PLANAR3, QK_ISO3, QK_PLANAR4, QK_ISO4 constants (append at end)
3. Copy quant implementation files: ggml-planar-quant.c, ggml-planar4-quant.c, ggml-iso-quant.c, ggml-iso4-quant.c into ggml/src/
4. Add function declarations to ggml-quants.h: quantize_row_planar3_0_ref, dequantize_row_planar3_0, quantize_planar3_0, etc. (append at end)

5. Add 4 type_traits[] entries to ggml.c (append in the array, after turbo entries, before GGML_TYPE_COUNT sentinel): each with .type_name, .blck_size, .type_size, .is_quantized=true, .to_float, .from_float_ref
6. Add 4 quantize_* dispatch cases to ggml.c's quantize switch (append before the F16 case): case GGML_TYPE_PLANAR3_0: result = quantize_planar3_0(...); break; etc.

7. Add 4 entries to the caps table in ggml-quant-caps.c (uncomment the planar/iso entries): each with .needs_wht=true, .needs_deferred=true, .k_cache_capable=true, .v_cache_capable=true, .head_align=128
8. Add the 4 new .c files to ggml/src/CMakeLists.txt
validation: No undefined reference errors (all quant functions linked)
grep -c 'GGML_TYPE_PLANAR3_0' src/llama-kv-cache.cpp returns 0 (no hardcoded checks needed — caps-driven)

phases.name: port_deferred_allocation
phases.description: Port the deferred F16→quant K-cache allocation and convert_deferred_keys() method. This is now FULLY data-driven by caps->needs_deferred. The code lands cleanly because kv-cache.cpp was already refactored in Phase 2 to use caps.

kv_layer_struct_fields.add_declaration:
Add to the public section of llama_kv_cache class:
    bool convert_deferred_keys();

convert_function.description: Append convert_deferred_keys() implementation at end of file
convert_function.implementation: See source: llama-cpp-turboquant-merged/src/llama-kv-cache.cpp lines 2858-2914. Copy verbatim. The function iterates layers, checks k_needs_convert, reads F16 → F32 → quantizes via from_float_ref → writes to k_quant → swaps tensor pointers.

validation: grep -c 'k_is_deferred' src/llama-kv-cache.cpp returns >= 3 (allocation + stream views + layer setup)
Functional test: load a model with -ctk planar3_0, verify prefill succeeds and convert_deferred_keys() returns true

phases.name: port_weight_compression
phases.description: Port weight compression modules. Weight quants use the same ggml_type enum and type_traits[] infrastructure, but are applied per-tensor during model loading (GGUF) rather than per-cache. They do NOT need caps entries unless they have special KV-cache behavior.
phases.scope: This phase is intentionally flexible. Weight compression quants (e.g., TQ3_1S, TQ4_1S, or any new weight quant) follow the same pattern as Phase 4: add enum, add block struct, add implementation .c file, add type_traits entry, add dispatch case. No kv-cache or graph changes needed.
phases.placeholder: Define specific weight quants to port based on requirements. Each follows the Phase 4 pattern.

phases.name: port_hrm_architect_and_hidden_state
phases.description: Port HRM (Hierarchical Recurrent Model) architect support and hidden state API. These plug into the existing llama_memory_i interface and model implementation layer. They are independent of the quant system.
phases.scope: HRM features use the llama_memory_recurrent interface (already exists for Mamba/RWKV models). Hidden state extraction uses the post-output-norm hidden state (already exposed in gemma4.cpp for MTP). These modules go in src/models/ and src/llama-memory-recurrent.*, NOT in ggml/.
phases.dependencies: Requires the kv-cache sharing architecture (mem_other, share callback) from TheTom's branch. Verify these exist in the base fork before porting.
phases.placeholder: Define specific HRM modules, hidden state API endpoints, and model implementations to port based on requirements.

phases.name: port_stability_modules
phases.description: Port stability modules (imatrix integration, perplexity monitoring, KL divergence testing). These are tooling/validation layers, not core inference path.
phases.scope: Goes in tools/ and common/ directories. Independent of quant system.
phases.placeholder: Define specific stability tools and metrics to port based on requirements.

future_quant_addition_workflow.description: How to add a new quant type after the modular system is in place
steps: 1. Add enum value to ggml.h (1 line, append before GGML_TYPE_COUNT)
2. Add block struct + QK constant to ggml-common.h (append at end)
4. Add function declarations to ggml-quants.h (append at end)
5. Add type_traits[] entry to ggml.c (append in array)
6. Add quantize dispatch case to ggml.c switch (append before F16 case)
7. Add caps entry to ggml-quant-caps.c (1 entry, set capability flags)
9. If CUDA support: add kernel files + fattn registration
